title: Which One Shipped?

narrative.intro: Three days before the investor demo, and there's been zero process - everyone just branches off whatever looked newest. Right now there are three builds sitting around: build-a, build-b, build-c. One of them is what actually got shown to investors. Which one?
narrative.correctDebrief: Correct - build-b. Every commit on it is signed, and the last one literally says it was approved for the demo. Notice what you had to do to figure that out, though: dig through commit messages and signatures by hand. That's the gap Configuration Identification closes - a real baseline would've just told you, instead of making you go forensic.
narrative.incorrectDebrief: Wrong build. Look again at which commits are actually signed, and which one has an explicit "approved for the demo" commit at its tip. This is exactly the failure mode Configuration Identification exists to prevent: without a labeled, approved baseline, "which one shipped" turns into a scavenger hunt instead of a lookup.

prompt: Which build actually shipped to the investor demo?
